title: Ultrafiltration and Purification of Conditioned Media Using Pall Jumbsosep and Izon qEV-10
author: Joshua A Welsh
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.beqnjdve
materials: Snap the reservoir onto the receiver
Unscrew the top cap from the column

steps.title: Prepare Filtered Ethanol
steps.instruction: Prepare 70% ethanol using HPLC or other pure water and filter at least 20 mL through a 0.02 µm syringe-driven filter (or another small pore size filter).

steps.title: Assemble and Sterilize Jumbosep Device
steps.instruction: Assemble the Jumbosep device and perform an ethanol sterilization and PBS flush.

substeps.instruction: Place a Jumbosep insert into a Jumbosep sample reservoir without contacting the inside of either component.
Use the blunt end of an aspirating tip to firmly push the insert into place.
Fill the reservoir with at least 10 mL of the prepared filtered 70% ethanol.
Swirl the device to maximize ethanol contact and let sit for 5 minutes.
Spin at 2500 RCF for 5 minutes (using a swinging bucket rotor and adaptor) to concentrate ethanol down to the 5 mL dead volume.
Separate the device by removing the reservoir cap and pressing the reservoir lip upward and backward.
Flush the reservoir with ~10 mL of sterile PBS and aspirate all volume from the receiver.
Reassemble the device, add 60 mL of sterile PBS to the reservoir, and spin at 3000 RCF for 5 minutes.
Aspirate all volume from the receiver.
Place the reservoir cap onto the reservoir and blot any fluid from the rim of the reservoir and receiver with a tissue.

steps.title: Harvest and Clear Conditioned Media
steps.instruction: Harvest cell culture media (when cells are 50% to 80% confluent, typically 48 hours post-seeding in phenol-red-free, bovine EV-depleted complete media) and clear it of debris.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the complete volume of media from each flask to a sterile 50 mL conical tube using a 50 mL serological pipet tip.
Spin tubes at 500 RCF for 10 minutes.
Transfer supernatants to new 50 mL conical tubes, leaving behind the cell/debris pellet.
Spin tubes at 2500 RCF for 10 minutes.
Transfer supernatants (leaving 1 to 2 mL at the bottom) to a sterile media storage bottle.

steps.title: Ultrafiltration of Conditioned Media
steps.instruction: Concentrate the cleared conditioned media using the Jumbosep device.

substeps.instruction: Wipe two 750 mL centrifuge bucket inserts and the insides of the buckets with 70% ethanol.
Load conditioned media into the reservoir up to the 60 mL mark.
Spin at 3000 RCF for ~20 minutes until only ~5 mL dead volume remains.
Disassemble the device, aspirate the filtrate, and reassemble.
Repeat the loading and spinning process (3000 RCF for 30 minutes at room temperature) until all media is processed. Increase centrifuge time by 5 to 10 minutes per additional spin if necessary.
If the final volume is less than 60 mL, add PBS to reach the 60 mL marker.
Perform a final wash: fill the reservoir with 60 mL of PBS to resuspend material, and spin at 3000 RCF at RT until ~5 mL dead volume remains.

steps.title: Recover and Store Concentrate
steps.instruction: Recover the concentrated media and store it temporarily.

substeps.instruction: Use a P1000 micropipette to thoroughly resuspend the concentrate on top of the insert in the sample reservoir, avoiding bubbles.
Transfer the ~5 mL concentrate to Eppendorf Low-protein binding 5.0 mL tubes (max 4 mL per tube).
Label and store at 4 ˚C overnight; do not store for long periods without further purification.

steps.title: Prepare qEV-10 Column
steps.instruction: Prepare the qEV-10 column for loading.

substeps.instruction: Remove a qEV-10 column from 4 ˚C storage and allow it to warm to room temperature.
Position the column vertically using a ring stand and metal clamp.
Rinse 5 mL of PBS from a new bottle through the loading chamber into waste.
Fill the column with PBS.
Press the loading chamber into the top of the column to ensure a tight seal.
Fill the loading chamber to the top with PBS.
Unscrew the bottom cap to allow PBS to flow into waste.
When half the PBS volume has flushed through, refill the loading chamber to the top with PBS.
While flushing, label 14 low protein-binding 5.0 mL Eppendorf tubes (fractions 1-14) and mark the 5.0 mL graduation.

steps.title: Load and Elute Media
steps.instruction: Load the concentrated media onto the column and collect fractions.

substeps.instruction: Once PBS has finished eluting, place the 'Fraction 1' tube under the column.
Gently vortex and invert the concentrated media; add it to the loading chamber 1 mL at a time, pipetting directly onto the reservoir filter (not the walls).
Immediately after the media passes through, fill the loading reservoir to the top with PBS.
Collect fractions in 5.0 mL increments, refilling the loading chamber when the PBS level drops by half.
Close tube lids once all PBS has flushed through into the waste container.

steps.title: Clean and Store Column
steps.instruction: Clean the column and prepare it for storage.

substeps.instruction: Add 5 mL of filtered 0.5 M NaOH to the chamber (pipetting along the walls) and allow it to pass through.
Fill the buffer reservoir to the top with PBS and allow it to pass through, leaving the last ~1 mL to prevent drying.
Refill the buffer reservoir to the top with PBS.
Verify the eluting buffer is neutral using a pH test strip.
Flush the column with 5 mL of filtered 20% EtOH.
Replace the bottom cap.
Fill the column to the top with filtered 20% EtOH using a pipette.
Replace the top cap.
Allow the loading chamber to dry in the hood overnight.
Return components to the box and label with date, cell line, and volume of concentrated media loaded.
